msgs.title: Some traders open a position every morning and close it every evening, and call it activity.
msgs.pub:
Some traders open a position every morning and close it every evening, and call it activity.

Penelope did it on purpose.

Waiting for Odysseus, she told the suitors she would choose once she finished a shroud.

She wove by day and pulled the threads out by night.

For her, undoing the work was the plan. It bought time.

For a trader, it buys commissions and fatigue.

Every rebuild costs spread and a little conviction.

If you are waiting, wait in cash.

Do not weave and unweave the same idea.

msgs.pub:
Watch how fast a rally you missed turns into a bubble.

Aesop told it with a fox.

He jumps for the grapes, falls short, and walks off saying they were sour anyway.

Markets are full of foxes.

Funds that stayed underweight. Bears who called the top twice.

Each one now explains why the move is not sustainable.

Maybe it is a bubble. Sometimes the fox is right.

Before I call a top, I picture myself long.

If the call vanishes, it was the fox talking.

msgs.pub:
The cheapest time to buy what everyone will want is winter, when nobody wants it.

People mocked Thales for being a poor philosopher.

So one winter he put small deposits on every olive press around Miletus.

Nobody bid against him. The presses sat empty and the harvest was months away.

Then the harvest came big, and every grower needed a press at once.

Thales set the price.

Today the hot names get the bids and the dull capacity gets ignored.

I would rather put a small deposit down in the quiet season than pay full price in the rush.

The deposit is small. The wait is the real cost.
